nodes.text: here's what the final script ended up looking like - for each username/password pair:

subNodes.text: using python's socket module, create a socket and connect to the picoCTF instance
receive the next 10KB of data from the socket
send the current username + "\n" to the socket
receive the next 10KB of data from the socket
send the current password + "\n" to the socket
receive the next 20KB of data from the socket

within this final 20KB, we have the password that was echoed back at us by the server, as well as the very last line, the "Invalid username or password" line. or, in the case of a successful run, something different.
we run this 20KB through a simple filter - does it contain "Invalid username or password"? if it does then scrap it. if not, echo out that last 20KB.

subNodes.text: ok, so our endpoints are:
GET / - just returns an HTML form that lets us upload a file
POST /upload - takes our file, stores it in redis as file|<id, an auto-incrementing integer>; the stored value in redis is JSON.stringify([filetype, base64 of file data]).
the file expires after 10 minutes
once the file is uploaded you get redirected to /paper/id.
GET /paper/:id - fetches the corresponding file from redis, decodes the base64, and serves it back with whatever content-type it was originally uploaded with
GET /secret -
reads the value of the "secret" cookie set on your browser as well as a "payload" query param
serves <body secret="your secret cookie val">(secret val) (payload)</body>
GET /flag - takes query param "secret", compares it to the current val in redis as key "secret", and if they're the same, it hands us the flag.
the key gets deleted on read so we only have one shot at getting the secret right
GET /visit/:id
this is the puppeteer endpoint
if no browsers are open, it calls visit("https://web/paper/<id>") where id is our file
THIS is our key to solving this challenge
the visit function:
first it generates a random 32-hex-char secret
it sets a cookie in the browser called "secret" to that 32-char value, sameSite:strict and domain: web
stores the same secret in redis with key "secret", which expires after 60 secondss
opens chrome and visits your uploaded file at "https://web/paper/<id>"
sleeps for 61 seconds and then closes chrome, deletes the redis key, basically resets
so what makes this hard is:
CSP says no javascript, so that's pretty messed up
chrome's URL blocklist is gonna be blocking everything but "https://web" so we need to stay within the internal network, but we also can't visit any data:// or file:// or anything like that
we only get 60s to get the flag once the secret exists
/flag deletes the secret on read so it's literally u get it or u dont

TL;DR: the redis LRU eviction settings in this box are set at a small enough size that it IS feasible to just stuff the database full of random shit and exceed that size. the problem with the css attribute selector trick was that we couldn't exfiltrate any data because we couldn't send anything other than GET requests. what these guys did was upload a bunch of oracle files to the database and then ran the bot with the same CSS trick, and then in that time, stuffed the database with enough random shit that every oracle that hadn't been visited got evicted. from there they were able to figure out what files still remained and reconstruct the flag with that information.
